opus.problem: Nearly the same fact as clue 5: being chosen as one of the twelve apostles. The night of prayer adds setting but nothing about this man, so the clue fits any of the twelve equally.
Fits any of the eleven apostles in the upper room equally. Nothing in the clue singles out this word, so it does not truly point to it.
Repeats the 'one of the twelve' fact from clues 4 and 6. Its only distinct detail is a list position, which overlaps clue 4's pairing with Thomas.

Beyond the call and the meal, the Bible gives few distinct facts about this word. Four of the seven clues (4 to 7) are versions of 'listed among the twelve.' Unused facts include being called Levi son of Alphaeus (Mark 2:14) and leaving everything behind (Luke 5:28). If those still don't give 7 different facts, the rules say to swap the word for a spare.
